journey.what_happens: Landing page. Both primary CTAs say 'Join the waitlist' and go to /mira/signup, not to plans.
Waitlist form. Native POST, works without JS. Not a purchase.
Live grounded demo chat. Answers only from the curated KB, remembers the visitor across visits, speaks with ElevenLabs TTS.
Four tier cards rendered from the single tier source. Each links to /mira/checkout?plan=<id>.
Five-step persona builder: Name, Vibe, Role, Channel, Review. WhatsApp is shown but disabled ('Coming soon').
journey.state_change: localStorage mira_setup; on submit a connect record via /api/begin

journey.what_happens: Posts to /api/begin. Mints an HMAC connect token, stores the persona, returns a Telegram deep link. Touches no payment provider.
Customer can type a discount code. The validator refuses every code by default and the checkout call never forwards one.
Server validates email, requires DODO_PAYMENTS_LIVE=1 plus the plan's product id, creates a Dodo subscription payment link and redirects.
Customer pays. Dodo is the merchant of record. No trial period is sent in the create-subscription body, though the UI promises 14 days free.
Return URL. Reads /api/connect?token= for display state and shows the Telegram button plus a three-step 'what happens next'.
Standard-Webhooks signature verified against the raw body, deduped on webhook-id, then subscription.active / renewed / payment.succeeded activate the tier.
journey.state_change: ConnectRecord status=active + subscription record + email->customer index

journey.what_happens: Deep link binds the chat. Single-use claim: the first telegram id owns the token, any other id is rejected 409. Bot authenticates with x-mira-bind-secret.
journey.state_change: ConnectRecord.telegramId set, status pending->bound; engine tenant created with the purchased tier

journey.what_happens: Mira introduces herself. This greeting is forced to voice regardless of the ratio, so it is the only TTS a customer reliably hears.
respond() runs: crisis check, moderation, canned/chat/job classify, memory, LLM with failover, leak filter, quota debit. Replies are capped at 160 tokens.
journey.state_change: 20-turn memory window, credit debit, token meter

journey.what_happens: Voice note downloaded and transcribed by ElevenLabs STT, then fed into the same pipeline.
Intended as a tier lever (1-in-5 free, 3-in-5 Studio). replyN is reset to 0 on every inbound message, so the ratio test is always false.
Image goes through tier-metered OCR (local tesseract, or the paid AFAQ engine on paid tiers) and the extracted text feeds the reply. Over-cap gets a warm limit message.
/help /whoami /tenant /switch /organizations /phone /privacy /unlink. Lazily loaded so a broken router can never take the bot down; runs after the entitlement gate and before any model call.
journey.state_change: varies by command; /unlink and /phone touch identity rows

journey.what_happens: Classified as a job, charged a 400+ credit affordability gate, answered 'On it', then the executor import fails because the bridge directory does not exist.
journey.state_change: job row created, then crash line delivered

journey.what_happens: Sold on the Companion tier. The retrieval side exists, but the only writer of tenant KB text has zero callers anywhere in the repo, so the KB is structurally empty.
Enter email, receive a single-use 15-minute magic link. Always answers 200 so the endpoint cannot enumerate accounts. Rate limited per IP and per email.
Renders from the server session only. Shows the plan, billing portal, cancel and refund controls — but entitlement is resolved from Stripe, and production charges through Dodo.
The route itself resolves the subscription from the Dodo-populated store by verified session email and cancels at period end. But the button is only rendered inside the Stripe-entitlement branch.
Records the request to an append-only JSONL file and emails the operator. Deliberately never calls the payment provider; a human approves.
Sold on the Studio tier and shown as 'Coming soon' in the persona builder. A provisioning gateway exists but nothing in the purchase flow reaches it.

features.name: Tier catalog
features.one_line: One tier source feeds /mira, /mira/plans and /mira/account; engine token caps match it exactly.

features.name: Dodo checkout
features.one_line: Live money path. Fails closed without a real email and without DODO_PAYMENTS_LIVE=1.

features.name: Dodo webhook activation
features.one_line: Raw-body signature check, id dedupe, activates or cancels the tier; 500s without marking so Dodo retries.

features.name: Stripe webhook (legacy)
features.one_line: Still wired and functional, but Dodo replaced Stripe as the merchant of record for new purchases.

features.name: Stripe billing portal
features.one_line: Opens a Stripe portal for known Stripe customers only; a Dodo-only customer has no record and is refused.

features.name: Magic-link sign-in
features.one_line: Single-use 15-minute token, non-enumerable responses, rate limited, sets an httpOnly session.

features.name: Entitlement resolver
features.one_line: Resolves 'has this person paid' from Stripe only — so a Dodo-paying customer resolves to no active plan.

features.name: Self-serve cancel
features.one_line: Session-only identity, no caller-supplied id to tamper with, cancels at period end.

features.name: Refund request
features.one_line: Durable append-only request plus operator email; refunding stays a human decision.

features.name: Discount codes
features.one_line: Kill-switched off by default because it validated against Stripe while charging through Dodo.

features.name: Connect token bind
features.one_line: HMAC-verified, single-use claim that ties a web purchase to one Telegram chat.

features.name: Persona builder
features.one_line: Name, vibe, role and channel captured on the web and carried to the bot at /start.

features.name: Grounded demo chat
features.one_line: Answers only from a curated public KB, remembers the visitor, refuses everything outside it.

features.name: Demo voice output
features.one_line: ElevenLabs TTS with per-IP and global daily caps; degrades to browser speech, never 500s.

features.name: Waitlist capture
features.one_line: Durable append-only JSONL outside the deploy tree, so a redeploy cannot wipe signups.

features.name: Contact form
features.one_line: Same durable JSONL pattern as the waitlist.

features.name: Support order lookup
features.one_line: Read-only view of the signed-in customer's own plan; takes no parameter, so there is nothing to enumerate.

features.name: Customer-service bot replies
features.one_line: Regex-matched canned answers; its own comment says wire it to the engine and verify the session later.

features.name: Admin control plane
features.one_line: Per-admin password then mandatory MFA, RBAC permissions, session revocation, separate from customer auth.

features.name: Tamper-evident admin audit
features.one_line: Append-only audit trail with chain verification; no route anywhere edits or deletes a row.

features.name: SEO + sitemap
features.one_line: Host-split sitemap and canonical helpers for vualet.com and mira.vualet.com.

features.name: Mira product storefront
features.one_line: Lists five family products with honest Free / Available / Coming soon badges.

features.name: Mira Writing (desktop)
features.one_line: Storefront links to an external download host; nothing in this repo builds, serves or verifies it.

features.name: Mira VPN
features.one_line: Preview page only; the page itself states no access links are being issued.

features.name: Mira ScreenWatcher
features.one_line: Storefront card with no destination link.

features.name: Mira Locksmith
features.one_line: Storefront card with no destination link.

features.name: Customers page
features.one_line: Honest placeholder: says 'Coming soon' rather than inventing testimonials.

features.name: respond() pipeline
features.one_line: The one live message pipeline for every channel; replies capped at 160 tokens.

features.name: Message classifier
features.one_line: Routes canned/chat/job, but sends 'write me', 'design' and 'make' to the build path that cannot execute.

features.name: Canned smalltalk cache
features.one_line: Zero-cost replies for greetings; keeps the cost floor honest.

features.name: Crisis interrupt
features.one_line: Self-harm detection with hotlines, ahead of everything else in the pipeline.

features.name: Inbound moderation
features.one_line: Hard refuse categories before any model call.

features.name: Provider-name scrubber
features.one_line: Substitutes the literal word 'me' for a matched provider name, producing sentences like 'I use me for that'.

features.name: Conversation memory
features.one_line: 20-turn rolling window plus a lossy LLM bullet summary — not correctable, not exportable, not a ledger.

features.name: Monthly token quota
features.one_line: Per-tenant monthly cap enforced from the single cap table; unknown tiers are spared rather than wrongly capped.

features.name: Image and document OCR
features.one_line: Local tesseract for everyone within a cap; the paid AFAQ engine only for paid tiers. The one true capability gate.

features.name: Voice note transcription
features.one_line: ElevenLabs STT on every inbound Telegram voice note.

features.name: Voice replies by tier ratio
features.one_line: The reply counter is reset on every inbound message, so the ratio test can never be true below 1.0.

features.name: Telegram command router
features.one_line: Eight commands, pure and injected, lazily loaded so a broken router cannot take the live bot down.

features.name: Tool-calling engine
features.one_line: A complete multi-round tool loop with four registered capabilities, and zero production callers.

features.name: Application build pipeline
features.one_line: Loads its executor from a bridge directory that does not exist on this machine, so every build crashes.

features.name: Job queue, concurrency, workspace, budget
features.one_line: Sound orchestration — atomic reservations, per-job path isolation, budget meter — wrapped around a missing executor.

features.name: Credit meter
features.one_line: Named 'ledger' but stores money, not the customer's information; trims to the last 1000 events.

features.name: Per-tenant knowledge base
features.one_line: Ingest and retrieve work, but the only writer has zero callers, so every tenant KB is permanently empty.

features.name: LAP grounding + output firewall
features.one_line: Grounding rows are never injected and three of four checks cannot alter output; the one live branch tells customers their own memory is false.

features.name: Style imitation
features.one_line: Runs on every reply without consent; can truncate answers to 30 characters or wrap them in 'Sure, ... right?'.

features.name: Approval gate
features.one_line: The right state machine pointed at prose styling instead of actions; nothing can enrol, approve or reject today.

features.name: Identity, orgs, consent
features.one_line: Migration and bridge exist and the bot loads them lazily, but the tables are not in the production database.

features.name: Hash-chained tenant ledger
features.one_line: The real context ledger the product is named for. Migration written; writes are hard-gated behind content encryption.

features.name: Content-at-rest encryption
features.one_line: Per-tenant wrapped DEK design is written; the table has never existed in production.

features.name: Behaviour facts store
features.one_line: Opens a local SQLite file while the system is Postgres; its table is in no migration and its schema init is never called.

features.name: WhatsApp provisioning gateway
features.one_line: Per-tenant isolated sessions with a branded pairing page; unreachable from any purchase, and headless WhatsApp breaks their ToS.

features.name: Android artifact delivery
features.one_line: A delivery mode whose function body is a single throw, with zero callers.

data_model.purpose: The bridge between a web purchase and a Telegram chat: token, plan, email, status, customerId, subscriptionId, telegramId, persona.
Upstash REST, else a durable JSON file, else in-process memory with a loud production warning. Live payments are gated on durability.
Reverse index so a signed-in customer can find their own subscription from their session email alone. Without it there is no cancel path.
Append-only durable stores for waitlist, contact messages and refund requests, kept outside the deploy tree.
Per-visitor durable memory for the public demo, keyed by a vd_visitor cookie.
The engine's customer row: tier, credits ledger_json, kb_json, voice_ratio, usage counters.
Build-job records. Builds only — there is no general task or commitment table.
Captured conversation content; the raw material a real ledger would be built from.
Style imitation and its unusable approval workflow.
kb_json, tokens_used_period, period_start, ocr_used_period, ocr_premium_used_period. Present in production.
Per-tenant wrapped data encryption key; the KEK lives only in an env var. NOT PRESENT in production.
Shared world facts and role seed libraries for the LAP grounding tiers. Neither is populated.

data_model.entity: identities, channel_identities, orgs, memberships, consents, invitations (008)
data_model.purpose: The identity and authorization layer. Written additively with no ALTER on tenants. Not yet in production.
The real hash-chained per-tenant context ledger. Statements are specified as ciphertext and the hash covers the stored bytes.
Append-only operator audit with chain verification and no edit or delete route.

open_gates.what: Migration 005 (tenant_deks) has never run in production, so content-at-rest encryption is not live.
open_gates.why_blocked: Production mira_state predates 005. The table is simply absent; the deployed engine is older than the migration.

open_gates.what: Shadow ledger writes must not be enabled before 005 is applied and DEK retrieval works.
open_gates.why_blocked: tenant_facts.statement is ciphertext and the hash covers the stored bytes, so plaintext written now can never be re-encrypted without breaking the chain irrecoverably.

open_gates.what: The first production restart applies SIX migrations (002, 005, 006, 007, 008, 009), not the two the deploy plan names.
open_gates.why_blocked: The plan's wording is wrong. All six were proved together on a snapshot, so the tested path is the real one, but sign-off must state the true blast radius.

open_gates.what: Production still runs roughly 2026-07-14 engine code; main is at 411ab1e and has never been deployed.
open_gates.why_blocked: Deploy is manual SSH with no auto-deploy, and the box holds a built image with no git checkout, so the deployed commit is not recoverable from the machine.

open_gates.what: Sign-in entitlement is resolved from Stripe while production charges through Dodo.
open_gates.why_blocked: entitlementForEmail queries Stripe only. A Dodo-paying customer who signs in sees 'No active plan', and the cancel and billing controls are inside that same branch — so the working cancel route is not reachable from the UI for them.

open_gates.what: The discount-code field is visible on checkout but every code is refused.
open_gates.why_blocked: The validator prices against Stripe while the charge goes through Dodo, and /api/checkout never forwards the code. It was quoting discounts it could not honour, so it was killed by default.

open_gates.what: Checkout promises a 14-day free trial; the Dodo create-subscription body sends no trial parameter.
open_gates.why_blocked: If a trial exists it is configured on the Dodo product, which cannot be verified from this repo. Unverified either way — treat as unproven until a live smoke purchase confirms it.

open_gates.what: No build can complete: the executor is imported from a bridge directory that does not exist.
open_gates.why_blocked: Either vendor the pipeline into the repo so it is version-controlled and testable, or replace it with the in-repo tool-calling loop that is already written.

open_gates.what: The one live LAP branch tells a customer their own memory is false.
open_gates.why_blocked: The tenant KB is structurally empty because its only writer has no callers, so the closed-world negative fires on every first-person question. It must be off until a populated ledger exists.

open_gates.what: No real card has been run end to end: pay, welcome, Telegram bind, webhook tier activation.
open_gates.why_blocked: Needs one live smoke purchase. Until then the activation chain is proven only by tests, not by a customer.

counts._reading: 34 of 53 features run today. The 19 that do not cluster in one place: doing the work for the customer (tool loop, build executor, task surface) and remembering the customer (tenant KB, hash-chained ledger, content encryption). Those are the two things the product is named for.
